assertions.subject: Humanitarian access: separate legal framework from operational feasibility
assertions.proposition: The ICRC explains that parties have primary responsibility for civilian basic needs under their control. Relief requires concerned parties’ consent, but consent is not wholly discretionary; after consent, parties must allow and facilitate relief, subject to a right of control.
conditions: Attributed summary of an ICRC legal explanation; application depends on conflict classification and facts. This is not legal advice or permission to operate. Lack of consent does not itself establish that withholding it is lawful; applicable duties depend on conflict and circumstances, including occupation. The source is an institutional explanation, not treaty text or a case-specific opinion.

evidence.evidence/34b04bfe141b60f0b39f251a12ef298:
The ICRC explains that parties have primary responsibility for civilian basic needs under their control. Relief requires concerned parties’ consent, but consent is not wholly discretionary; after consent, parties must allow and facilitate relief, subject to a right of control.
Qualification: Attributed summary of an ICRC legal explanation; application depends on conflict classification and facts. This is not legal advice or permission to operate. Lack of consent does not itself establish that withholding it is lawful; applicable duties depend on conflict and circumstances, including occupation. The source is an institutional explanation, not treaty text or a case-specific opinion.
Primary sources: https://www.icrc.org/en/document/humanitarian-access-what-law-says
evidence.evidence/86aeea27a18772c39b120f48a01d216:
The ICRC describes controls such as searches, routes and timing, while warning against controls that unduly delay relief or make it impossible.
Qualification: Do not turn this summary into a finding that a named actor violated law. Permissible control in general does not establish that a particular restriction is lawful.
Primary sources: https://www.icrc.org/en/document/humanitarian-access-what-law-says
evidence.evidence/477999d041bcc36dece254fa4507fee:
OCHA’s toolbox describes monitoring access constraints, their effects, restrictive policies and mitigation actions through an access-monitoring framework.
Qualification: A framework description, not current incident data or evidence that a particular route is accessible.
Primary sources: https://knowledge.base.unocha.org/wiki/spaces/imtoolbox/pages/1410072577/Humanitarian%2BAccess
